correctness.rationale: For every \(\lambda>0\), \(K=\sum_i v_i\) is linearly equivalent to both \(4v_2\) and \(4v_3\) by explicit integral-slope vertex potentials. The unique real potential for \(4v_2-4p\) exists by a positive-conductance weighted Laplacian and has integer slopes if and only if \(K\sim4p\). On all five unit-edge interiors an unavoidable slope is one of \(1-t\), \(1+t\) or \(-t\), hence nonintegral. On the variable edge, all slopes are integer affine expressions in \(k=(4t-3\lambda-1)/(2(\lambda+1))\); the exact strict bounds permit only \(k=-1\) or \(k=0\), and both are interior exactly when \(\lambda>1\). Endpoint tests give \(v_0,v_1\) precisely at \(\lambda=1\). All graph points are covered. A standard-library exact-fraction checker was executed successfully for eight rational lengths and all interior mesh points of spacing \(1/16\); this is a corroboration, not an all-real proof.

value.rationale: The equilateral metric \(K_4\) is a canonical tropical Weierstrass example, and deformation of a single edge is the minimal perturbation preserving most of its symmetry. The full real-parameter classification of the exceptional genus-three gap condition \((1,2,5)\), equivalently \(K\sim4p\), finds a sharp wall at \(\lambda=1\) and gives exact locations of two moving interior points on the long side. This provides a meaningful stability and boundary phenomenon for tropical degenerations, not a finite-table recomputation or an arbitrary parameter slice.
